I absolutely love this game.  It's one of the few games that I wanted to replay as soon as I beat it.

So I've played the game a couple times through now, and I have some thoughts on it (and some pretty fun experiences).

The game is very fairly priced, and has a good portion of content with a good selection of paths you can take, though they all end up the same place, which possibly could be a turn-off. I've seen a couple bugs here and there, but it wasn't very difficult to deal with, or never long enough in where I dreaded to restart.

The story is really cool, albeit kind of easy to predict. It's very immersing though, and really gets going at a rapid pace. I enjoy it time and time again, and take my time to do the missions properly, although I know most of them and know which ones are "skippable".

Now, mechanics wise.. It gets kind of weird. It's very easy to get into, and you can pick it up and play the game to a finish "fairly" easily, but that's where it gets interesting. There's lots of small mechanics and tweaks you can make to the gameplay (renaming all but PortHack, having a trap shell set on yourself at all times, ect.), which ends out in you being able to dive deeper into it than just doing the base game. And if you enjoy collecting the different skins, then you have a lot of work to do (Looking at you, CCC hacksquad).

Now, onto the DLC.

The DLC brings a lot of things to the table. Instead of the mailbox, you're now in a chatroom with three other hackers. This leaves a door slightly open to get some really decent hints if you're stuck, and the general descriptions of the missions make it a lot easier to understand what you're doing when playing through the content for the first time. It also brings new mechanics, in that the ports will now be changing ever so often, without warning (though that's not much of a challenge, as long as you look at the port #'s before pressing enter, you're good). Now I do have a single warning though, if you haven't played through the DLC before.

[b] Make sure to check if the CMD prompts are actual Windows prompts or in-game prompts.[b] I got a scare when I had just worked my way through the prompt, only for my pc to reboot when i put in 'shutdown /r'. Just close the game, that's more than enough.

Overall, 9/10. Would've loved for some more content, and some bigger challenges. I was hoping the DLC would go the extra mile above the base game, but it sadly didn't. I can definitely recommend the game if you're looking for something different and something to puzzle yourself with. It requires a fairly keen eye.

It tells a little story through email exchanges between more or less anonymous hackers and things discovered on hacked computers. The game also takes a refreshing approach to turning hacking into game mechanics that feel somewhat realistic. There are several instances where the game takes some liberties, but they all make total sense from a game perspective. A game where e. g. you'd spend days or weeks waiting for your custom malware to phone home to your command-and-control server would probably be pretty dull. Simplifying the subject matter in a way that makes it playable while at the same time retaining some of the right vibes, is definitely one of the merits of the game.

The story-telling does not work as well as that presentation of hacking activities. Without cutscenes, narration, inner monologue, exposition, you just get a couple of emails. And by the time the main quest-line kicks into high gear. you've kinda learned to read mails cursorily to find the quest objectives from a series of what are basically fetch-quests to build up your street cred. Add to that that you have no real exposition of the character you're playing, so there is no real emotional attachment and consequently (at least for me) no deep connection to the person you're finding out about. It's like: I know, I should care, but I don't really. Also, the premise of the main story is less realistic than other aspects of the game (security by obscurity is an illusion!).
Interestingly enough, it is a side quest that actually works best for me. It's  called Junebug. That quest is well written, gives the right vibes when it comes to doing your research (if hopefully not about how actual pacemakers are implemented), and lingers with you.

Me personally, I work on terminal sessions every day and don't really need a game for those vibes, and would rather just get on some coding project than play it. But other than that it's a nice little game that has enough merits for the low price, that you can enjoy for a couple of hours, and that even has an extension system that allows people to add missions and thus adds value beyond the base game itself.
